title: OpenAI Chat Completions Request (hermes-auto-router wire subset, v1)
description: The subset of the OpenAI Chat Completions request body that the local routing gateway accepts at POST /v1/chat/completions (design.md 5.3). The gateway must stay OpenAI Chat Completions compatible because Hermes's normal chat transport already sends OpenAI-formatted messages and tools. Unknown top-level keys are permitted (additionalProperties: true) because providers add fields and the gateway must forward requests it can still relay rather than rejecting them; every key this schema does define is strictly typed. Fields deliberately left untyped-but-accepted include n, presence_penalty, frequency_penalty, logit_bias, logprobs, top_logprobs, parallel_tool_calls, service_tier, store, metadata, reasoning_effort, modalities, audio, prediction, and the deprecated functions/function_call pair.

model.description: Requested model. For this gateway this is normally a virtual alias such as auto:balanced (design.md 5.1).

messages.description: Conversation so far, in OpenAI message order.

tools.description: Tool definitions available to the model for this turn.

stream.description: Whether the response is delivered as an SSE stream. Not required; both true and false are valid. When true the response is a sequence of chunks matching sse-stream-contract.v1.

stream_options.description: Streaming modifiers. include_usage requests a final chunk carrying token usage (design.md 20.3, 'usage in final stream chunks').

max_completion_tokens.description: Current output-token cap; supersedes max_tokens on newer models.

stop.description: One stop sequence or a list of them.

_hermes_auto.description: Routing metadata injected by the Hermes provider plugin via build_extra_body(). Referenced by $id rather than restated, so there is exactly one source of truth for its shape and the envelope's own rules — protocol_version must be 1, unknown keys are a version mismatch — are actually enforced here. Typing it as a bare object instead accepted {"protocol_version": 99, "junk": "x"}. Resolving this $ref requires the validator to carry a registry covering the routing schemas; hermes_auto.gateway.schemas.validate() builds one from the loaded mapping. Permitted but never required. Per design.md 5.1 the gateway strips this key before forwarding the request upstream.

message.description: One chat message. Tool results use role=tool and must carry the tool_call_id they answer; only assistant messages may carry tool_calls.

tool_calls.description: Tool calls emitted by the assistant. More than one entry represents parallel tool calls (design.md 20.3).

tool_call_id.description: Identifier of the assistant tool call this message answers. Required on role=tool messages.

messageContent.description: Message body: a plain string, null (assistant messages that only emit tool calls), or an ordered array of multipart content parts.

contentPart.description: One part of a multipart message body, dispatched on `type`. Image parts are what make the vision cases in design.md 20.3 expressible. This def is deliberately OPEN rather than a closed oneOf: a closed form was the only closed object in a relay schema whose message objects one level up are additionalProperties: true, and it rejected requests the upstream provider accepts — `cache_control` on a text part, `mime_type` on an image part, and the `input_audio` and `file` part types, the first of which is the only way the `audio` modality this schema claims to accept can actually arrive. Unknown part types relay untyped; the two types the gateway itself reasons about stay strictly typed via the conditionals below.

type.description: Part discriminator, e.g. `text`, `image_url`, `input_audio`, or `file`. Required and a string so a part is always dispatchable, but not enumerated, so a part type added by a provider is relayed rather than rejected.

url.description: An https URL or a data: URI carrying the image bytes.

toolCall.description: One assistant tool call. Note that function.arguments is a JSON-encoded string, not an object; that is precisely why streamed arguments arrive fragmented and must be concatenated before parsing (design.md 20.3).

arguments.description: JSON-encoded argument object, carried as a string.

parameters.description: JSON Schema describing the tool's arguments.

toolChoice.description: How the model should use tools: a mode keyword, or an object naming one function.

responseFormat.description: Structured-output request (design.md 20.3, 'structured outputs'). A `json_schema` type without its `json_schema` payload is not a relayable request — the upstream provider has nothing to constrain generation with — so the payload is conditionally required rather than merely permitted.

schema.description: The JSON Schema the completion must conform to.
